topic: Ocean resources and EEZ — mixed tiers
description: Fisheries, oil & gas, polymetallic nodules, EEZ, UNCLOS, marine pollution

questions.stem: Under UNCLOS (1982), a coastal state's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extends from its shore baseline to a maximum of:

options.option_text: 12 nautical miles (the territorial-sea limit)
200 nautical miles (about 370 km from the baseline)
350 nautical miles (only continental-shelf claim)
500 nautical miles (no such limit in UNCLOS)

questions.explanation: UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982) — defines maritime zones. Territorial sea: 12 nm (full sovereignty). Contiguous zone: 24 nm (limited control). EEZ: 200 nm (sovereign rights over economic resources — fishing, oil, gas, mining). Continental shelf: 200 nm or further if naturally extending (max 350 nm). India's EEZ ~ 2.3 million km² — among the world's largest. Distractor 1 = territorial sea. Distractor 3 = extended shelf claim cap. Distractor 4 = invented.

questions.stem: POLYMETALLIC NODULES on the deep-ocean floor are commercially valuable mainly for their content of:

options.option_text: Gold, silver, platinum traces only
Manganese, nickel, copper, cobalt
Lithium, sodium, potassium salts
Uranium and rare-earth elements only

questions.explanation: Polymetallic / manganese nodules — potato-sized rocks scattered on abyssal plains (~4-6 km depth). Composition: ~30% manganese, 1.3% nickel, 1.1% copper, 0.2% cobalt, plus iron + traces. Critical for batteries (Ni, Co), stainless steel (Mn), electronics. India has been allotted a 75,000 km² PMN exploration site in the Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB) by the International Seabed Authority — first developing country to get such allotment (1987). Deep-sea mining is technically feasible but environmentally controversial — ISA has not yet finalised commercial-extraction rules.

questions.stem: India's MAJOR offshore oil and gas field, accounting for ~40% of domestic production, is the:

options.option_text: Krishna-Godavari basin off Andhra coast
Bombay High in the Arabian Sea, off Mumbai
Cambay basin off Gujarat's western coast
Andaman offshore basin near Port Blair

questions.explanation: Bombay High — discovered 1974 by ONGC, ~160 km off Mumbai. Production began 1976. Single largest oil + gas field in India; offshore platform 'Sagar Samrat' was the rig. Krishna-Godavari (KG) basin (off AP coast) — major gas field; Reliance KG-D6 block. Cambay basin — onshore + shallow offshore Gujarat (small fields). Andaman basin — under exploration; potential not yet large. India imports ~85% of crude needs despite Bombay High; demand far exceeds domestic output.

questions.stem: The world's most productive marine fishing grounds typically occur where:

options.option_text: Two warm ocean currents converge over deep water
Cold and warm currents meet over a continental shelf
An equatorial current flows steadily eastward
Coral reefs form along tropical island shores

questions.explanation: Major fishing grounds — Grand Banks (Canada, Labrador-Gulf Stream meeting), Doggerbank (North Sea), Hokkaido (Oyashio-Kuroshio), Peruvian coast (Humboldt upwelling). Cold + warm currents meet → strong upwelling brings nutrient-rich deep water to the surface → plankton bloom → fish abundance. Continental shelves (< 200 m depth) provide ideal habitat. Distractor 1 — convergence of two warm currents creates a stratified, low-nutrient zone. Distractor 3 — equatorial currents are too uniform thermally. Distractor 4 — coral reefs are biodiverse but small in total fish biomass compared to temperate shelves.

questions.stem: The 'BLUE REVOLUTION' in the Indian context refers to:

options.option_text: Rapid expansion of inland water transport corridors
Rapid expansion of fish production from rivers and seas
Drinking-water coverage to every rural household
Cleaning the Ganga under the Namami Gange mission

questions.explanation: Blue Revolution — initiated under the Fish Farmers Development Agency (1973-74) and accelerated under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY, 2020). Aim: boost India's fish production. India is now the SECOND largest fish producer in the world (after China). FY24 production ~17 million tonnes. Major contributors: Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Gujarat. Other 'colour' revolutions: Green (foodgrain), White (milk — Operation Flood, Verghese Kurien), Yellow (oilseeds), Pink (onions/meat), Silver (eggs), Golden (fruits/horticulture).

questions.stem: The MARIANA TRENCH, the deepest known point in any ocean, is located in the:

options.option_text: South Atlantic Ocean near Antarctica
Western Pacific Ocean east of the Philippines
North Indian Ocean near Sri Lanka
Arctic Ocean near the North Pole region

questions.explanation: Mariana Trench — Western Pacific, east of the Mariana Islands, just east of the Philippines. Depth ~10,994 m at the Challenger Deep — deepest known point on Earth. Formed by the Pacific Plate subducting under the smaller Mariana Plate. First crewed descent — 1960 (Trieste — Jacques Piccard, Don Walsh). Second — 2012 (James Cameron solo dive). Other deep trenches: Tonga (~10,800 m), Philippine (~10,500 m), Java/Sunda (~7,400 m, deepest in Indian Ocean), Puerto Rico (~8,400 m, deepest in Atlantic).

questions.stem: The 'GARBAGE PATCH' in the North Pacific is primarily made up of:

options.option_text: Floating logs from large-scale rainforest deforestation
Tiny plastic fragments accumulated by ocean gyre currents
Toxic chemical sludge from offshore oil-rig leaks
Sunken cargo from container-ship spills near Hawaii

questions.explanation: Great Pacific Garbage Patch — between Hawaii and California; ~1.6 million km² (~3× the size of France). Composed mostly of MICROPLASTICS (1-5 mm fragments) plus larger plastic debris, fishing nets, bottles. Concentrated by the North Pacific subtropical gyre — converging currents trap floating debris. The water is not solid garbage as often imagined; it's a 'plastic soup' with high concentrations. Five major ocean gyres globally — each has a similar garbage patch (Indian Ocean, North Atlantic, South Pacific, South Atlantic). Plastic enters the food chain via marine animals; ~80% of marine plastic comes from land-based sources, primarily rivers in developing countries.

questions.stem: Which international body, established under UNCLOS, is mandated to regulate exploration and exploitation of mineral resources in 'The Area' — the seabed beyond any national jurisdiction?

options.option_text: International Maritime Organization (IMO), based in London
International Seabed Authority (ISA), based in Kingston, Jamaica
International Tribunal for Law of the Sea (ITLOS), in Hamburg
UN Environment Programme (UNEP), headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya

questions.explanation: The ISA, headquartered in Kingston, Jamaica, was established by UNCLOS Part XI to administer 'The Area' (seabed and subsoil beyond national jurisdiction) on behalf of mankind as a whole. IMO (London) handles shipping safety and marine pollution, not seabed mining. ITLOS (Hamburg) is a judicial body that settles disputes under UNCLOS but does not regulate resource exploitation.

questions.stem: Under UNCLOS, the 'contiguous zone' allows a coastal state to enforce customs, fiscal, immigration, and sanitation laws. Up to what distance from the baseline does this zone extend?

options.option_text: Up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline
Up to 24 nautical miles from the baseline
Up to 48 nautical miles from the baseline
Up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline

questions.explanation: The contiguous zone extends to 24 NM from the baseline under UNCLOS Article 33. The territorial sea ends at 12 NM (full sovereignty), the contiguous zone covers 12–24 NM (limited enforcement powers), and the EEZ extends to 200 NM (resource rights). 200 NM is a common wrong answer because students confuse the EEZ with the contiguous zone.

questions.stem: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) harnesses the temperature gradient between warm surface water and cold deep-ocean water. What is the minimum temperature differential (approximately) required for a commercially viable OTEC plant?

options.option_text: A differential of at least 5°C between surface and depth
A differential of at least 20°C between surface and depth
A differential of at least 40°C between surface and depth
A differential of at least 60°C between surface and depth

questions.explanation: A temperature difference of at least 20°C between warm surface water (~25–28°C) and cold deep water (~4–5°C at 800–1000 m depth) is the established engineering threshold for viable OTEC operation. This condition is met in tropical waters near islands like Lakshadweep, which is why India's OTEC pilot was proposed at Kavaratti. A 5°C differential is far too small to drive a thermodynamic cycle efficiently.

questions.stem: Which Indian programme has been at the forefront of exploring gas hydrate (methane clathrate) deposits in Indian waters, including the Krishna-Godavari Basin and Andaman Sea?

options.option_text: National Offshore Wind Energy Programme under MNRE
National Gas Hydrate Programme (NGHP) under MoPNG
Integrated Coastal Zone Management Project under MoEFCC
Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) under Ministry of Earth Sciences

questions.explanation: The NGHP (National Gas Hydrate Programme), coordinated by MoPNG with ONGC, GAIL, and Oil India as implementing agencies, has conducted two major expeditions (NGHP-01 in 2006, NGHP-02 in 2015) and confirmed world-class gas hydrate deposits in the KG Basin. The Deep Ocean Mission (DOM), though related to ocean science, focuses on deep-sea biodiversity, mineral exploration, and manned submersibles — not gas hydrates specifically.

questions.stem: Hydrothermal vents on the mid-ocean ridge known as 'black smokers' emit superheated mineral-rich water. The economically significant mineral deposits that precipitate around these vents are classified as:

options.option_text: Ferromanganese crusts deposited on seamount surfaces
Seafloor massive sulphide (SMS) deposits around vent chimneys
Phosphorite nodules concentrated in coastal upwelling zones
Polymetallic nodules scattered across abyssal plain sediments

questions.explanation: Black smokers precipitate Seafloor Massive Sulphide (SMS) deposits — rich in copper, zinc, gold, and silver — directly around vent chimneys as superheated water meets cold seawater. Polymetallic nodules (Mn, Co, Ni, Cu) form by slow precipitation on abyssal plains far from vents, making them the most tempting wrong answer. Ferromanganese crusts form on seamounts, and phosphorites occur in upwelling zones near continental margins.

questions.stem: Under Article 76 of UNCLOS, a coastal state may claim an 'extended continental shelf' beyond 200 nautical miles. What are the two alternative outer-limit formulae permitted by this Article?

options.option_text: Either 300 NM from baseline, or 50 NM beyond the 3,000 m isobath
Either 350 NM from baseline, or 100 NM beyond the 2,500 m isobath
Either 400 NM from baseline, or 150 NM beyond the 2,000 m isobath
Either 500 NM from baseline, or 200 NM beyond the 1,500 m isobath

questions.explanation: Article 76(5) of UNCLOS fixes the outer edge of the continental margin at whichever is more seaward: (i) 350 NM from the territorial-sea baseline, OR (ii) 100 NM from the 2,500-metre isobath (a specific depth contour). Claims must be submitted to and validated by the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS). India has submitted a partial claim for its extended shelf. The 300/50 option is a common false memory conflating the contiguous-zone logic.

questions.stem: India holds 'Pioneer Investor' status granted by the International Seabed Authority for polymetallic nodule exploration. In which oceanic basin has India been allocated an exclusive exploration block of approximately 75,000 sq km?

options.option_text: North-West Indian Ocean Basin near the Carlsberg Ridge axis
Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB), in the southern Indian Ocean
Andaman Basin adjacent to the Andaman–Nicobar island arc
Arabian Sea abyssal plain near the Laccadive–Chagos Ridge

questions.explanation: India's ~75,000 sq km Pioneer Investor block for polymetallic nodule exploration (Mn, Co, Ni, Cu) lies in the Central Indian Ocean Basin (CIOB), roughly between 10°S and 16°S latitude. This status, managed by NCPOR (National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research), gives India exclusive rights under ISA's 'parallel system' — half for the sponsoring state, half for ISA. The Andaman Basin is a back-arc basin and the Carlsberg Ridge hosts mid-ocean hydrothermal activity, both popular distractors but incorrect locations.
